title.reading: つきのいでたらむよは　じゅうごやずり
title.zh: 月出之夜 · 十五夜摺
title.en: On Nights When the Moon Comes Out — A Fifteenth-Night Impression

logline_zh: 十五夜，祖母以初升的明月为灯，把《竹取物语》化作纸门上的影绘；当月亮走进圆窗，她自己的影子离开身体，攀着窗格升入月中，只回头望了一眼。六十个秋天之后，当年的孩子白发苍苍，披着祖母留下的羽织独坐同一条檐廊，在一轮丝毫未老的月亮下把那一夜看完——正如辉夜姬所托：“有月亮出来的夜晚，请望向我。”
logline_en: On the fifteenth night a grandmother turns the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter into shadows on the shoji, with the rising moon as her lantern; when the moon reaches the round window, her own shadow leaves her body, climbs the lattice into it, and looks back once. Sixty autumns later the child, now old, sits alone on the same veranda in her grandmother's haori and finishes the night under a moon that has not aged — doing what Kaguya asked: on nights when the moon comes out, look toward me.
time_convention: Segment 'start'/'end' and every 't_abs' are absolute film seconds. In beats and text_cues, 't' is LOCAL seconds from the segment's start (this is what js/script.js and TSUKI.TEXT consume). Inside layer/moon prose, times are written as local seconds followed by absolute film time in brackets, e.g. '6.5s [124.5]'. In 'audio', 'summary', 'negative_space' and 'transition_out', all times are absolute film seconds.
device: The whole film is ONE woodblock print pulled on the Fifteenth Night, and its printing is the story. (1) 序 teaches the grammar: blank washi, a baren spiral reveals the sumi key block, each colour block lands a few px out of register and settles with a wooden kentō CLICK, and one round patch stays dry — the moon, which is never printed. (2) The grandmother's night (t 14–160) is the 初摺, the first impression: every block, crisp bokashi, fresh pigment. At the moon's culmination (140.0, exactly centred in the round window) the night hinges. (3) On the sōzu's KON at 160.0 the same master shot is pulled again from the worn blocks sixty years later — the 後摺: warm blocks gone, sky flat, key lines broken, registration drifted, paper yellowed and foxed. Only the moon is identical, because an absence cannot wear out. The second half of the moon's arc (culmination → set) belongs to this later night; the join is invisible because the moon does not change. (4) Renderer = plates: every master shot is cached as a key block + colour plates, each drawn per frame with a (dx, dy, alpha) from one table. The same table performs the printing (序), the tears — every colour plate drifting ±6–12 px while the key block holds — and the cold CLICK back into register at 147.8 (五), the jolt into the late impression (六) and the final unprinting in fugitive-pigment order (結). (5) Transitions between segments are never print-pulls: a seamless hand-off (序→一), sōzu-KON hard cuts (40.0, 160.0), a match-cut ring→basin (66.0), a fox-window iris (90–92), a suyari-gasumi wipe (118–121), a cut on falling hands (190.0) and a match-cut incense→Fuji smoke at the same x (206.0). (6) Three lenses show the myths without close faces: shoji shadow-play (影絵), water (水鏡), and the fox window (狐の窓), whose diamond clip in 六 re-renders the first-impression scene function at t − 150. (7) Six cached master shots (A wide garden, A′ engawa profile, B shoji wall with round window, C tsukubai, D straight up, E dawn Fuji); たけ and old 小夜 share one figure path. Thesis: お月見 is humanity doing what Kaguya asked — 月の出でたらむ夜は、見おこせたまへ — and those left behind remember on behalf of the one who was made to forget.

The yellowed paper of the 後摺 (sixty years later), applied as a multiply tint everywhere except the moon's disc.
Highlights, snow, the light through puppet slits, kumiko flashes during the climb, dango, kasumi bands, the ribbon of light (天の羽衣), mica (kira) sparkle base.

The key block, silhouettes, interior darkness, the black 叢雲. As 薄墨 (α 0.06–0.35): smoke, incense, the rabbit's maria (22%).
Clouds, geese, stone, Fuji's smoke thread, far susuki.
Drained colours after the robe; the dawn moon glaze; 後摺 susuki plumes; たけ's hair.
EVERY cast shadow on the shoji (never pure black): the shadow-play, the shadows cast by nothing, the climbing shadow, dawn shadows.
Night sky mid-tones, far hills, 小夜's kasuri kimono, たけ's kimono.
Sky bokashi; the ichimonji band (mixed with 墨 35%); Fuji's massif; Shot D's night.
Water (pond, tsukubai); the ground of the 波兎 haori; the flat pale sky of the 後摺 (α 0.45).
桔梗 flowers in the jug; the pre-dawn band above the 東雲.
Garden greens, susuki stems, moss, reeds, the 萩 branch's leaves.
Susuki plumes, thatch highlights, tatami, 衣かつぎ skins.
聚楽 plaster walls, thatch, earth, the unfaded rectangle; mixed with 墨 (55%) it is the 煤竹 of wood, posts and engawa boards.
The rising moon's glaze and horizon glow; andon-lit shoji; the fire's core; 女郎花; the 金 of mica (kira) palace in the fox window (at low alpha + sparkle).

ONE ink with two names: the 退紅 of the child's obi-age faded over sixty years (the single warm spot in the 後摺), and the 東雲 of the final dawn. The dawn is printed in the colour of the faded sash.

global_motifs: THE UNBROKEN MOON: one celestial arc for 236 s, never cut or reprinted, culminating exactly in the round window at 140.0 and sinking into Fuji's peak at dawn; it falls faster in old age.
THE MOON IS PAPER: never inked — a hole through every plate to the washi — except the rabbit's maria, printed from smoke at 106.0 and kept by every later moon. The rabbit earned it.

初摺 / 後摺: the grandmother's night is the first impression (all blocks, bokashi, fresh pigment); sixty years later is a late impression from the worn blocks (warm blocks gone, flat sky, broken lines, drift, foxing). The moon alone is identical in both, because an absence cannot wear out.
MISREGISTRATION = TEARS, CLICK = FORGETTING: the kentō click learned in 序 returns once, at 147.8, when perfect register means the robe has erased her grief.

COLOUR STAYS ON EARTH: the drain turns たけ to 胡粉/銀鼠 while the haori and the child's 紅 obi-age keep their colour; in the 後摺 the only warm colour left is that obi-age faded to 退紅, tying the susuki — and the dawn is printed in the same ink.

SHADOW = SOUL, LIGHT = ABSENCE: Kaguya in the shadow-play is a hole cut in paper; the celestials are shadows cast by nothing; たけ's shadow leaves her body; afterwards she casts no shadow while the child does.
ONLY SMOKE REACHES THE MOON, and only once: the smoke chain — 衣かつぎ steam → the rabbit's pyre → 叢雲 → incense → Fuji's undying smoke, which touches the moon at 214.0.
THE 縁 MOTIF broken on its fifth note at the CLICK and completed sixty years later by the shakuhachi — the one left behind finishes the phrase.
INSECTS ARE THE EARTH'S HEARTBEAT: silent at the leap and under the cloud, returning one by one; the film ends on a single suzumushi.
PRETENDING NOT TO SEE: お月見泥棒 at 33.0 (たけ turns to the moon) is inherited at 198.5 (小夜 turns to the moon) — the fox is the thief the second time.
THE FOX WINDOW: たけ shows the child the moon's true face (三); sixty years later the old hands show the old woman her own first night, still playing in colour (六).
THE SECOND TEACUP: two cups poured, one untouched with a tiny moon in it — rhyming with the ladle-moon of 三 and with the scroll 掬水月在手. Never explained.
THE 形見: Kaguya's letter asks that the robe she leaves be kept as a keepsake; on screen it is たけ's 波兎 haori, laid over the sleeping child, worn by her for sixty years. 羽織 quietly rhymes with 羽衣.
THE HELD-BACK BELL: no 梵鐘 until dawn; its hum is tuned to the note the shakuhachi finally supplies.
金木犀 florets (桂花 / 月中桂) drift through the first night — a wordless bridge for the Chinese viewer, alongside 掬水月在手, 邵雍's 月到天心処 behind Buson, and Bai Juyi's 故人.

moon_clock.rule: The moon is ONE unbroken celestial arc for the whole film, never cut, never re-printed. Its angle φ(t) is a monotone cubic (PCHIP) through the keypoints; each master shot projects φ with its own mapping, so the moon may sit in different screen places in different shots but its sky position, size law and colour are continuous. Rise (t 16) → culmination inside the round window (t 140.0) takes 124 s; culmination → set into Fuji's peak (≈t 218.5) takes only ≈78 s: the moon falls faster in old age (time dilation, cf. 「月はやし」).

mappings.A: x = 960 − 800·cosφ ; y = 700 − 560·sinφ ; r = 72 + 38·(1 − sinφ)²  (horizon illusion: r≈121 at rise, 72 at culmination)
mappings.A_prime: Moon off-frame (upper right); only its light direction matters: shadows fall to the lower left.
mappings.B: Moon glow behind the shoji paper: centre x = 960 − 420·cosφ, y = 960 − 810·sinφ, radial bokashi r 220. The disc itself (r 64) is visible only through the round window (centre (960,150), r 110): fully inside for ≈t 131–146, exactly centred at t 140.0.
mappings.C: Reflection only (art-directed): ellipse rx 70 ry 40 at (1000,600) in the tsukubai.
mappings.D: Looking straight up: fixed at (960,430), r 260, 月暈 halo ring r 420.
mappings.E: Dawn (art-directed): r 48, from (1110,250) at t 206 straight down to (1180,330) at t 214.0 (lower rim y 378 meets the smoke tip), resting on the summit ≈t 216 (パール富士), sunk into the peak by t 218.5.

moon_clock.colour: φ < 0.3: 山吹 glaze α = 0.55·(1 − sinφ) over the bare paper; 0.3–2.7: bare 生成 with a 月白 glaze α 0.2; φ > 2.7: 銀鼠 glaze rising to α 0.5, kira fading.
moon_clock.rendering: Destination-out hole through every ink plate down to the washi, plus a kira band (soft 胡粉 'lighter' stripe, 30 px, 30°) sweeping across the disc every 7 s. The face is BLANK until t 106.0; from then on the rabbit's maria (墨 α 0.22, a separate 'rabbit plate') are the only ink ever laid on the moon. In the 後摺 the moon's disc is exempt from yellowing and wear: it is the one fresh thing in the late impression. After the final unprinting it survives as a karazuri (blind-embossed) circle carrying the rabbit's faint carbon (α 0.10).
moon_clock.law_of_contact: Nothing touches the moon except once: Fuji's smoke at t 214.0. Clouds may pass in front of it; the incense (七) and every other smoke must stop short.

plates.state: Every plate is drawn from its per-shot cache with a per-t (dx, dy, alpha). The moon's disc is cut out of every plate (destination-out). One table drives: the printing in 序, the tears and CLICK in 五, the 後摺 state and its jolt in 六, and the unprinting in 結.
plates.shozuri: 初摺 (first impression, t 0–160): all plates on, registration within ±0.5 px, crisp bokashi, fresh pigments, 生成 paper.
plates.atozuri: 後摺 (late impression, t 160–236): P2 alpha 0 (except the single hand-applied 鴇/退紅 spot on the cord); P6 printed flat with NO bokashi and NO ichimonji at α 0.55 and offset (+5,−3); P5 offset (+5,−3); K with seeded dash-gaps (≤ 8% of length) and a few cracks; stronger goma-zuri speckle; paper 生成 × 鳥の子 multiply + ~60 foxing dots (煤竹 α 0.12–0.25). Restraint: it must read as an old print, not a broken render.
plates.jolt: t 160.0–160.6: each plate performs a damped oscillation of amplitude 4–8 px (seeded direction, 3 cycles), P2 rises 4 px as its alpha falls to 0, key-line gaps and yellowing ramp 0→1.
plates.tears: t 140.0–147.8: offsets P1 (0,+12), P2 (+10,+4), P5 (−12,−6), P6 (+6,−10), P7 (−4,+8), P4 (±3 only, so the climbing shadow stays legible), K holds at (0,0). Each is multiplied by ramp(140→142)·sin(2π(t−140)/3.1 + 1.3·i). The misaligned holes give the moon chromatic fringes (藍 on the left, 山吹 on the right, 1–4 px).
plates.click: t 147.8: every plate snaps to (0,0) within 60 ms, no overshoot. Perfect register = the loss of feeling.
plates.unprint: t 222.0–228.0, in the real order fugitive pigments fade: D + P2 (鴇/東雲, 紅, 朱, 山吹, 萩) 222.0–223.5 → P5 + P6 (blues) 223.5–225.0 → P1 + P3 + P4 (earths, greens, greys) 225.0–226.5 → K last 226.5–228.0 (carbon never fades). Each group slips 2–4 px out of register and rises 4 px as its alpha falls to 0. The rabbit plate R stays at α 0.10.

sound_bible.scale: 都節 (miyako-bushi / in) on D: D–E♭–G–A–B♭. Koto in 平調子 on D.
sound_bible.en_motif: The 縁 motif, A4–B♭4–D5–E♭5–D5 (the E♭ reached by oshide press from D). Stated WHOLE only once, at moonrise (t 16.5–19.9). During the climb (140–147.8) the koto forgets it in four passes; it breaks off at the CLICK on the rest where the fifth note (D5, 'home') should fall. At 210.5 the koto offers the first four notes again; at 214.0 the SHAKUHACHI — the voice of the one left behind — plays the missing D5 as the smoke touches the moon, and the dawn bell's hum (tuned to D) sustains it.
sound_bible.earth_heartbeat: Insects are mortal life. Suzumushi ('rīn': 4.2–4.6 kHz sine carriers, 30–40 Hz AM trill) and matsumushi ('chin-chirorin', ≈3.5 kHz, 3-note pattern). They stop for 1.2 s at the rabbit's leap (99.0–100.2), thin out as heaven arrives (132–140), vanish entirely under the cloud (148.0–152.0, absolute silence) and return one at a time (156.6, 158.2). In the 後摺 only three remain, then two, then one. The last sound of the film is a single suzumushi (233.0).
sound_bible.heaven: Shō aitake cluster A4 B4 E5 F♯5 A5 B5 (no semitones: heaven has none), breath-swelled; kagura-suzu shimmer (inharmonic 3–9 kHz); the fox-window glass cluster A6 B6 E7.
sound_bible.punctuation: Sōzu KON (200 Hz sine thump + wood click, big room reverb) at 40.0 (cut to the theatre), 160.0 (sixty years pass) and 232.5 (the water has returned); a dry sōzu in 六 and a dew 'plink' at 201.5. The kentō CLICK (1.2 kHz woodblock tick, 12 ms + 180 Hz thunk) is taught in 序 as the sound of a block landing in register and returns once, at 147.8, as the sound of forgetting. The 梵鐘 is WITHHELD for the whole film until dawn: three strokes of 明け六つ at 215, 220, 225 (additive inharmonic partials 0.5, 1, 1.18, 1.5, 2.0, 2.74, 3.76 over a D hum, one pair detuned 0.7 Hz for 唸り, 12 s decay).
sound_bible.instruments: Koto (Karplus-Strong; 後摺 = higher loss, shorter decays), shakuhachi (sine + band-passed breath, meri/kari bends, muraiki onsets), biwa (Karplus-Strong + sawari noise buzz) for the shadow-play, shō (additive cluster), kagura-suzu, soft taiko (55–90 Hz sine thumps), small 鏧 bowl (only at the rabbit's leap), wind in susuki (pink noise 0.8–2 kHz, seeded gusts), water (trickle, drops as gliding sine pings), geese (two-formant FM honks), paper (baren rub, brush swishes, peel swishes).
sound_bible.silences: 0–2 (paper), 99.0–100.2 (the leap: only the bowl), 148.0–152.0 (absolute: master gain 0), 234.2–236.0 (end).
sound_bible.scrubbing: Continuous beds read their parameters from t; discrete events come from a sorted event list and are rescheduled from the current t on every seek.

text_style.fonts: Japanese vertical (writing-mode: vertical-rl): Shippori Mincho B1 for poems and narration; Yuji Syuku for the title and for Kaguya's letter. Chinese: one small horizontal line in Noto Serif SC in the subtitle band y 960–1040.
text_style.seals: Classical texts: a small 朱文 seal 「月」 (red characters). 小夜's original haiku: a 白文 seal 「小夜」 (white characters in red ground) — the film is quietly her 句集. Title: 「縁」. Final stamp on the paper (canvas, not DOM): 朱 「忘れじ」 ≈90 px at (1300,820), t 230.0.
text_style.rules: 14 text blocks in 236 s. Never two on screen at once; ≥ 1.5 s between cues; every haiku/waka/kanshi on screen ≥ 8 s. No text at all during the climb, the cloud and the colour drain (140–160). Text reveal and fade are computed from t (engine TEXT.update), never CSS animation. 'ink': light = 胡粉 on dark grounds, dark = 墨 on paper. When a cue sits on a painted cartouche (短冊/色紙), the SCENE draws the cartouche panel on canvas for the cue's exact interval; the DOM draws only the characters.
text_style.positions: Engine positions (css/film.css): right / upper-right / left / upper-left / center; every cue here also gives explicit x,y (left/top of the text block in logical px) to land in the shot's text pocket.

segments.summary: The film is pulled like a woodblock print. Blank washi; a baren spirals out from the thatched house and reveals Shot A in sumi only; the colour blocks drop in one by one, each landing a few px out of register and settling with a wooden kentō click. Before any colour is laid, one round patch above the susuki stays dry and glows 山吹: the moon exists before the world is printed. The title writes itself — a sentence that stops halfway.
segments.time_of_night: dusk before moonrise (宵, ≈17:50 on 十五夜)

moon.phase_note: full (十五夜) but not yet risen: only a dry, unprinted disc cut out of every plate and a 山吹 glow bokashi above the susuki mark where it will rise
moon.motion: none; the glow breathes ±6% on a 7 s period from 6s [6]

layers.name: washi
layers.description: Blank 生成 paper, full frame (the engine adds fibres and mottling). This scene adds a 40 px ragged deckle at all four edges and the 見当: a karazuri L-mark (鉤見当) at (1840,1040), arms 46 px, drawn as a 1 px 胡粉 highlight above-left and a 1 px 墨 α 0.12 shadow below-right.
layers.motion: 0.8s [0.8] the notch catches raking light (highlight α 0.2→0.6→0.35 over 1.2 s). Deckle visible to 6s [6], fading into the normal frame by 9s [9].

layers.name: key block (墨)
layers.description: The complete Shot A line-work in 墨 α 0.85: house, thatch hatching, shoji kumiko, engawa, pond rim, sōzu, susuki plume lines, Fuji contour, 萩 branch. No fills.
layers.motion: 2s [2]–6s [6] revealed through a baren mask: an Archimedean spiral centred on the house (1180,560), stroke width 150 px, reach r(t) = 1300·inOutSine((t−2)/4); goma-zuri speckle (seeded 1–2 px gaps, 6%) where the spiral overlaps itself.

layers.name: colour plates
layers.description: Shot A's plates in printing order (see plates): P1 黄土, P2 warm (紅/萩/山吹), P3 松葉+尾花, P4 greys, P5 藍 pond, P6 ベロ藍 sky with ichimonji and horizon bokashi, P7 胡粉/月白, P8 kira.
layers.motion: Plate i lands at 6s [6] + 0.55·i (i = 0…7): α 0→1 in 0.12 s from a seeded offset of 4–6 px, easing to (0,0) with outCubic over 0.45 s; the kentō click sounds as it touches. P6's ichimonji band is wiped left→right 8.9s [8.9]–9.5s [9.5].

layers.name: the moon before the moon

beats.desc: Blank washi. Paper room tone only.
The 見当 notch catches the light.
The baren begins: sumi lines spiral out from the house.
The first colour block (黄土) lands 5 px out of register and settles — click. One circle above the susuki stays dry: the moon's place.
The title begins to write itself.
The ベロ藍 sky lands; the ichimonji band is wiped across the top.
Mica lands; the print sparkles faintly.
The first suzumushi, far away.
The first gust in the susuki: the print is alive.

text_cues.reading: つきのいでたらむよは　じゅうごやずり
text_cues.source: Title taken from Kaguya-hime's farewell letter in 『竹取物語』 (「月の出でたらむ夜は、見おこせたまへ」), deliberately stopped halfway.
text_cues.zh: 月出之夜 · 十五夜摺
text_cues.en: On Nights When the Moon Comes Out — A Fifteenth-Night Impression
text_cues.note: Column 1 (Yuji Syuku) sits on the 短冊 panel x 1680–1790; column 2 十五夜摺 is set small in the 色紙 x 1560–1660, y 60–160. Seal 「縁」 at the tanzaku's foot. The sentence is completed on screen at 122.5 s by the letter.

segments.negative_space: Upper-right x 1540–1830, y 50–480 (title tanzaku + 色紙) is flat ベロ藍 sky only; Fuji's peak (1720,500) sits just below it. The dry moon circle (x 40–300, y 580–820) must never be covered. Subtitle band y 960–1040 = pond: calm.
segments.audio: 0–2: near silence (paper room tone, brown noise −50 dB). 2.0–6.0: baren rub — band-passed brown noise 300–1200 Hz whose gain follows the spiral's speed, in 0.7 s circular strokes. 6.0–10.2: eight kentō clicks, one per plate (1.2 kHz woodblock tick, 12 ms, plus a soft 180 Hz thunk). This exact click returns at 147.8 as the sound of forgetting, so it must be clean and memorable. 7.0: one koto 引き色 — D4 plucked, then pulled ~40 cents flat — as the title lands. 12.0: first suzumushi (single far voice). 13.0: first susuki gust (pink noise 0.8–2 kHz swell).
segments.transition_out: Seamless hand-off (0 s): the last frame of 序 is Shot A 初摺 fully printed and 一 begins on the identical frame. The title fades 12.4–14.0 (engine fade 2.0 s).
segments.hero_image: 4.2s [4.2] — Shot A half-born: sumi lines have spiralled out from the thatched house across half the sheet; the rest is blank washi with its deckle and registration notch; above the unprinted susuki a round patch of paper glows faintly 山吹 — the moon before the world.
segments.simplification: Cache Shot A's key block and each colour plate once (they are reused by 一, 四 and 六). The reveal is a mask canvas (the spiral stroked with round caps, lineWidth 150) applied with destination-in; plate landings are drawImage with (dx,dy,alpha). No per-frame blur.

segments.summary: First impression. A huge 山吹 moon rises through the susuki with a blank face; six-year-old 小夜, carrying susuki taller than herself, crosses the disc — the poster frame. Two eye-glints in the grass: the fox. She runs the pond rim (Bashō's 'all night long', as delight) while grandmother たけ builds the 三方: fifteen dango, one per koto pluck, stacked 9-4-2; 衣かつぎ steam for 芋名月; the autumn grasses in a jug; a few 金木犀 florets drift past. お月見泥棒: a small arm steals a dango and たけ turns to the moon and pretends not to see. She blows out the andon; the shoji turn moon-white; the theatre opens. KON.

moon.phase_note: full; blank uninked face; warm 山吹 glaze at the horizon cooling toward bare paper

layers.name: far land
layers.description: Low 紺 hills y 580–640 (no key line). Fuji small, peak (1720,500), flanks reaching y 620 at x 1500 and 1940, flat ベロ藍 with a thin 胡粉 first-snow line 6–10 px under the peak, half-hidden by the kasumi.

layers.name: 萩 branch
layers.description: Foreground frame across the top-left (x 0–380, y 0–260): tapered 墨 stems, 松葉 leaflets, 萩 blossom clusters.

layers.name: 金木犀
layers.description: Three osmanthus florets (4-petal crosses, 4 px, 朱 with 山吹 centres).

beats.desc: The print breathes: wind, the insects gathering.
The moon's rim rises through the susuki — huge, 山吹, blank. The 縁 motif sounds whole on the koto (16.5–19.9): the only complete statement in the film.
小夜 emerges from the susuki with a sheaf taller than herself.
Two eye-glints in the grass — the fox. A blink at 21.2; gone at 22.0.
POSTER FRAME: the tiny child silhouetted on the gold disc.
小夜 runs the pond rim; たけ begins the 三方.
Dango appear one per pluck: nine … four … two (to 29.4).
金木犀 florets drift across the 萩 branch.
衣かつぎ set down; steam rises (芋名月).
小夜 sets susuki, 萩, 女郎花 and 桔梗 in the jug.
お月見泥棒: a small arm from below the engawa takes the top dango. Fourteen remain.
たけ turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see.
The andon is blown out; the shoji turn from 山吹 to 月白; the moon is the only light.
A slow push toward the shoji (scale 1.00→1.06 about (1180,630)).
The sōzu tips.
KON — hard cut.

text_cues.reading: めいげつや　いけをめぐりて　よもすがら
text_cues.author: 芭蕉
text_cues.source: 松尾芭蕉　貞享三年（1686）八月十五夜、深川芭蕉庵の月見にて　『孤松』所収
text_cues.zh: 明月当空——绕着池塘走啊走，走了一整夜。
text_cues.note: On screen 小夜 is literally circling the pond: Bashō's delight. The poem's 'all night long' is the film's own time-scale (one night, twice).

segments.negative_space: Sky pocket x 500–860, y 60–580 (between the 萩 branch and the house) holds only flat bokashi for the haiku. The rising moon at far left (x 40–320) must never be covered. Subtitle band y 960–1040 = pond: keep moon-road dashes sparse there (α ≤ 0.35).
segments.audio: Wind in the susuki (pink noise band-passed 0.8–2 kHz, gusts at 19.5, 27.0, 35.0). Insect chorus builds: suzumushi 1→8 voices by 30 s; matsumushi 3 voices from 24 s. Sōzu trickle (narrow-band noise). 16.5–19.9: the 縁 motif WHOLE on koto, rubato — A4 16.5 · B♭4 17.2 · D5 17.9 · E♭5 18.8 (oshide from D5) · D5 19.9, long decay. 22.4–29.4: fifteen koto plucks, one per dango — the counting melody in miyako-bushi: D4 E♭4 G4 A4 B♭4 A4 G4 E♭4 D4 | G4 A4 B♭4 D5 | E♭5 D5. 33.0: paper rustle; 33.6: a single koto harmonic (the grandmother's complicity — this exact harmonic returns at 198.5). 37.0: a breath puff (0.3 s) and the andon flame gutter. 40.0: sōzu KON — 200 Hz sine thump + wooden click, long room reverb; every bed cuts with it.
segments.transition_out: Hard cut on the KON at 40.0 (0 s) to Shot B interior; the last 2 s push slowly toward the darkened shoji so the cut feels like stepping inside.
segments.hero_image: 7s [21] — a vast 山吹 moon cut by silhouetted susuki plumes; across its lower third a tiny black child carries an over-tall sheaf of susuki; a 萩 branch hangs in from the top-left under a ベロ藍 ichimonji band (homage: 武蔵野図屏風; 芳年『月百姿』).
segments.simplification: Far/mid susuki, hills, Fuji, house and pond body come from the cached Shot A plates; only the near susuki, figures, dango, steam, glints and moon road animate. Figures are CAST.elder / CAST.child at small scale; dango are circles; the 9-4-2 stack is a fixed coordinate list revealed by count(t).

segments.summary: Inside, the andon out. Four moon-white shoji are the screen and the rising moon is the lantern. On the engawa outside, たけ holds paper cut-outs in the moonlight; inside, 小夜 kneels with her back to us and watches the Tale of the Bamboo Cutter play across the panels right to left, like an emaki. The shining node is a slit in the paper; the princess is a hole in the shape of a girl — light is made of absence. One continuous morph grows her from a three-inch child into a woman with floor-length hair. An emperor's palanquin passes. Under the real glow she raises her sleeve to her face; 小夜 looks up toward the round window; and たけ lifts a paper moon until it eclipses the real one — 'looking at the moon's face is forbidden'.

moon.phase_note: not seen directly: a radial glow through the paper of panels 1–2 (r = glow radius); the round window shows only 紺 sky
moon.motion: Shot B mapping: glow centre (573,645) 0s [40] → (650,414) 26s [66]; 21.5s [61.5]–24.5s [64.5] a paper moon's shadow slides over it until only a ring of light remains.

layers.name: interior
layers.description: Room darkness: 墨 at the top grading to 煤竹 (黄土×墨) at floor level. No detail.

layers.name: upper wall & round window
layers.description: 小壁 y 40–260, x 300–1620: 聚楽 plaster (黄土 with 鼠 grain, α 0.55 in the dark). Round window centred (960,150), r 110, 墨 rim 8 px, 葭 reed lattice (墨 1 px verticals every 9 px, two horizontals); behind it 紺 sky, no moon yet.

layers.name: shoji
layers.description: Four panels x 300–630, 630–960, 960–1290, 1290–1620, y 270–960. 月白 paper lit from behind by the moon glow (radial bokashi: 月白 at the glow centre falling to 月白×藍鼠 50% on the far panels). Kumiko 3 × 6 cells (≈110×115) per panel in 墨/煤竹 4 px, frames 10 px; central stile x 960.
layers.motion: The glow centre wanders with φ.

layers.name: shadow-play
layers.description: 藍鼠 multiply, never black. Puppet shadows are sharp (penumbra 1 px: the cut-outs are held against the paper); たけ's body and arm shadows are soft (6–10 px). The tale reads RIGHT→LEFT: panel 4 bamboo, panel 3 growth, panel 2 palanquin, panel 1 Kaguya. Kaguya is always a 'negative puppet': a dark cut-out field with her figure cut out of it, so she is made of the paper's light.

layers.name: offering shadow
layers.description: Bottom-left of panel 1 (x 330–560, y 820–960): the tsukimi still-life in shadow — a stepped pyramid of fourteen circles on the 三方 and the jug with a susuki spray.

layers.name: たけ's shadow
layers.description: Bottom-right, x 1300–1500, y 700–960: her bent profile with the bun, the puppeteer; her forearms rise into the panels holding sticks.
layers.motion: body still; arms lift and carry the puppets at each beat

layers.name: tokonoma
layers.description: Left edge x 40–250: tokonoma post (墨) and wall; hanging scroll x 110–180, y 300–820 on a 生成 mount with 黄土 border, one column of 墨 calligraphy 「掬水月在手」 (于良史「春山夜月」; visual only), dim at α 0.35 in the spill light.

layers.name: tatami
layers.description: y 960–1080: 尾花×鼠 tatami with 墨 heri lines converging on (960,540) (uki-e perspective).

layers.name: 小夜 (foreground)
layers.description: Back view, kneeling seiza, x 860–1060, y 900–1080: a 墨 silhouette with the okappa bob and a thin 紅 obi-age line catching the light.
layers.motion: 18.5s [58.5] her head tilts up 14° toward the round window; 21.5s [61.5] lowers.

beats.desc: Cut in on the KON. The shoji are cold 月白; the insects are muffled by the walls.
たけ's shadow lifts three paper culms into panel 4: a bamboo grove in sharp shadow. The biwa opens the tale.
The bamboo-cutter puppet (60 px) walks in along the bottom rail of panel 4.
One node shines: a slit in the puppet lets the moonlight through — a 胡粉 point with kira.
The axe-shadow swings; the culm splits; inside stands a girl-shaped hole of light, 26 px tall.
たけ's hand-shadow carries her into panel 3. ONE CONTINUOUS MORPH (50.5–54.5): child → girl → young woman with hair to the floor, always a hole of light in a dark oval cut-out.
(Optional) Panel 2: an emperor's palanquin (鳳輦, phoenix finial) crosses right→left, pauses 0.6 s, moves on.
Panel 1, under the real glow: Kaguya — light in the shape of a woman on a cut-out engawa — raises her sleeve to her face (1.5 s).
In the foreground 小夜 tilts her head up toward the round window.
The whisper appears: 「月の顔見るは、忌むこと」.
たけ raises a paper-cut full moon on a stick; its dark shadow slides in from the right over the real glow. 小夜 lowers her head.
Alignment: a black disc ringed with light — an eclipse made by a grandmother's hand.
Slow push-in on the ring (scale 1.00→1.08 about its centre) to set up the match-cut.

text_cues.reading: つきのかおみるは、いむこと
text_cues.author: 竹取物語
text_cues.source: 『竹取物語』「ある人の『月の顔見るは、忌むこと』と制しけれども、ともすれば、人間にも月を見ては、いみじく泣きたまふ。」
text_cues.note: たけ's warning, quoted from the tale; small and pale (薄墨 feeling: 胡粉 at 70%). It lands as the paper moon covers the real one.

segments.negative_space: Right wall x 1640–1900, y 100–820 (dark, beyond panel 4) stays unlit and plain for the text. Subtitle band y 960–1040: tatami and 小夜's dark back only.
segments.audio: Insects muffled (low-pass 1.5 kHz, −9 dB). Biwa plucks (Karplus-Strong + noise-burst sawari) on each shadow beat: 41.0, 43.0, 46.0, 48.0, 50.5, 52.5, 54.5, 57.0. Paper rustles at each puppet change. 46.0 and 48.0: kagura-suzu shimmer. 50.5–54.5: a rising koto arpeggio across the growth (D4→D5, miyako-bushi). 55.0–57.0: soft taiko steps, two per second (the palanquin). 57.5–61.0: shakuhachi meri sigh — E♭4 bending down to D4, breath audible. 64.5: at the eclipse the mix dips −6 dB and a low koto D2 is plucked and left to ring.
segments.transition_out: Match-cut at 66.0 (0 s): the eclipse ring — a bright annulus round a dark disc — cuts to the tsukubai's stone rim round its dark water, placed where the ring was after the push-in.
segments.hero_image: 24.5s [64.5] — four moon-white shoji; on the left panel a luminous girl-shaped hole with her sleeve to her face beneath a black paper moon ringed with light; at right the bent shadow of the old puppeteer; in the foreground the small dark back of a kneeling child; the dim scroll 掬水月在手 at the edge.
segments.simplification: Every shadow is one flat 藍鼠 fill (multiply); penumbra = 2–3 offset low-alpha passes, not blur. Puppets are simple paths; the negative puppet is one path filled evenodd. The growth morph = three authored silhouettes with equal vertex counts (96), lerped. Base outlines from CAST.okina, CAST.kaguya ('weep') and CAST.elder. The palanquin is the first thing to cut.

segments.summary: At the tsukubai the child grabs the moon in the water and it shatters into mica. The ripples die; the moon returns, untouched. たけ's ladle lifts a tiny moon and tips it into the child's cupped hands; the moon leaks away between her fingers until her hands are dark and empty — her first lesson in transience, which she will write down sixty years later. Then たけ interlaces her old fingers into the fox window: inside the diamond the moon shows its true face — a palace roofline in mica and a rabbit in blind embossing. Still no ink.

moon.phase_note: only as a reflection: an elliptical hole to paper (rx 70, ry 40) in dark water with a kira glint; a tiny moon (r 18) in the ladle and the child's palms; inside the fox window, the true moon (r 130)

layers.name: ground

layers.description: Stone ellipse 720×420 centred (960,620): 鼠 with a 墨 key line, 黄土 lichen flecks, a 月白 highlight along the far rim.

layers.name: water
layers.description: Ellipse 560×300 centred (960,620): 藍 with ベロ藍 bokashi toward the far edge; the reflected moon at (1000,600) as a hole to paper with kira; ripple rings as concentric 月白 arcs (α 0.4) in the seigaiha manner.
layers.motion: A drop lands at (700,580) every 2.3 s (first 0.3s [66.3]); rings expand 60 px/s and fade over 2 s.

layers.name: spout
layers.description: Bamboo 筧 from the left edge (0,470) to (690,560): 松葉/尾花 cylinder, 墨 nodes; drops as 胡粉 beads r 3.

layers.name: petals
layers.description: Six 萩 petals floating (ovals 6×3).

layers.name: shards
layers.description: ≈40 seeded crescents (胡粉 + kira) made from the reflection.
layers.motion: 1.5s [67.5] fly apart (eased drift up to 180 px); 4s [70]–6s [72] regather exponentially (τ 0.6 s).

layers.name: hands & ladle
layers.description: Silhouettes (墨) entering from outside the frame: 小夜's small hands from the bottom; たけ's knuckled hands and the ladle (柄杓: 煤竹 handle, 黄土 cup, 墨 key) from the top-right; at 84–90 the edge of her 波兎 sleeve (藍 with one 胡粉 rabbit).

layers.name: fox window
layers.description: Diamond clip (an even-odd hole in the hand path) centred (960,420), ≈300×230. Inside: 紺 sky, the moon r 130 as a hole to paper, a palace roofline across its lower third in mica only (山吹 α 0.3 + sparkle), and a rabbit in karazuri relief (±1.5 px light/dark rim, NO ink — the rabbit has not yet earned its place).
layers.motion: 18s [84]–19.5s [85.5] the hands interlace; the inside is revealed 19.5s [85.5]; 22s [88] the diamond begins to grow (the engine iris continues it into 四).

beats.desc: Cut in on the stone rim: the reflected moon whole in dark water. A drop falls (66.3).
Small hands plunge in; at 67.5 the moon shatters into some forty mica shards and the rings race outward.
The hands come up empty and dripping, bright beads falling.
The ripples die away; the shards regather; by 72.0 the moon is whole again, untouched.
たけ's ladle enters from the top-right, dips (73.5), lifts (74.5): a tiny moon in its cup.
She tips it into 小夜's cupped hands.
The moon sits in the child's palms. Beads fall between her fingers every half-second; the moon shrinks with the water, r = 18·(1−(t−77)/7)^0.7.
The small hands tremble.
The last drop. The hands are dark and empty.
たけ's old hands interlace into the fox window (狐の窓) and hold it before the child's eye.
Inside the diamond, the moon's true face: a palace roofline of mica, a rabbit in blind relief.
The diamond begins to open — an iris into the sky.

text_cues.reading: すくいたる　つきこぼれけり　このてより
text_cues.author: 小夜
text_cues.zh: 舀起的月亮，从孩子的手心洒落了。

segments.shot: D, then tilt down to A
segments.summary: Looking straight up: an enormous blank moon with a halo. On its paper face, in sumi, the Jataka plays: an old beggar, a monkey with fruit, a fox with a fish, a rabbit with nothing. A fire is lit — the only warm colour ever drawn inside the moon. The rabbit looks up and leaps. The disc flashes white and every insect on earth stops for 1.2 s. The smoke drifts across the face and settles into a rabbit pounding with pestle and mortar: the maria are born, the only ink ever laid on the moon, and every moon afterwards keeps it. The pestle's ぺったん fades as we tilt down to earth, where たけ gives her own dango to 小夜 and the child falls asleep in her lap.

beats.desc: The iris completes: an enormous blank moon, a halo, the tips of susuki.
On the moon's face a beggar shuffles in and sits.
A monkey brings fruit; a fox brings a fish; the rabbit searches and comes back with nothing. Its ears droop (95.5).
The monkey gathers sticks; the fox lights them: the fire — the only warm colour ever drawn inside the moon.
The rabbit looks up — out of the moon, at us.
It leaps in a parabola into the fire.
The disc flashes 胡粉 for 0.4 s. Every insect on earth stops (99.0–100.2).
The beggar rises; his outline turns to mica (帝釈天) and fades with the monkey and the fox (100–103).
Smoke spreads across the blank face and begins to gather.
The insects return, one at a time.
The maria are printed: a rabbit with pestle and mortar — the moon's only ink.
ぺったん: the pestle begins, every 1.6 s.
Tilt down to earth; with every metre the pestle grows fainter until it cannot be heard (≈112).
The shō enters, pianissimo.
たけ gives 小夜 her own dango.
The child leans into her lap and falls asleep (115.5).

segments.audio: Insects continue (6 voices) until 99.0. The play on the moon is narrated sparsely: 92.0 a biwa pluck (the beggar); 93.5 and 94.2 two light koto notes (monkey, fox); 95.5 a low descending pair (the empty-handed rabbit). 95.5–99.0 fire crackle (seeded noise bursts). 97.5 a single high koto harmonic as the rabbit looks up. 98.9 a hard biwa bachi strike at the leap. 99.0 ALL INSECTS STOP for 1.2 s; in the gap only one small struck bowl (鏧, ≈1.1 kHz inharmonic, 6 s decay). 100.2 onward the insects return voice by voice (100.2, 100.6, 101.1, 101.9, 103.0). 106.4 ぺったん every 1.6 s — a soft taiko thump (90 Hz sine, 0.15 s) + a hand-slap noise, doubled by the lowest koto D2; from 108.0 its gain falls with the tilt, 1.0 → 0 by 112.0: the pestle we stop hearing (no text says so). 110.0: shō aitake cluster (A4 B4 E5 F♯5 A5 B5) enters pp.

segments.hero_image: 16s [106] — an enormous paper-white moon with a faint halo against ベロ藍; thin 薄墨 smoke has just settled into a rabbit pounding at a mortar; the last ember fades at its centre; black susuki plumes stand along the bottom edge.
segments.simplification: The 300 particles exist only in Shot D (≤ 16 s); targets are sampled once at init with isPointInPath on a grid; paths are analytic (eased lerp + curl-noise offset) so each frame is a pure function of t; after 106.0 draw the baked maria bitmap instead. The tilt is two cached masters translated vertically.

segments.summary: The climax. Inside again: the moon climbs into the round window. On the shoji, たけ's shadow lifts her haori against the light — for two seconds its rabbits-over-waves pattern shines through — and lays it over the sleeping child: the robe left behind as a keepsake, while Kaguya's letter completes the film's title. Then shadows cast by nothing: a cloud of celestials slides down the paper though the garden is empty, and a ribbon of light — the heavenly robe — unfurls down the central stile. At the moon's culmination her shadow peels off the paper, straightens out of old age and climbs the lattice rung by rung, while every colour plate drifts out of register like eyes filling with tears and the koto forgets its melody. She looks back once. CLICK — perfect register, cold: she has forgotten. She enters the moon; a black cloud covers it; absolute silence. When it passes, only the child's shadow remains under the haori's. Outside, たけ sits upright with her eyes closed; a wave drains her colour to moon-white while the haori and the child's red sash stay bright. The child casts a shadow; the grandmother casts none. One cricket. Then another.

layers.motion: 38.4s [156.4]–40.8s [158.8] COLOUR DRAIN: a feathered horizontal wavefront descends through たけ, top to bottom — 紺→月白, 黄土→胡粉, 朱→胡粉, 煤竹→銀鼠, key lines 墨→銀鼠 — with kira along the front. The haori and the obi-age keep full saturation.

beats.desc: Through the mist wipe: Shot B. The glow has climbed to the top of the shoji. The shō, pianissimo.
The moon's rim enters the round window.
たけ's shadow slips off her haori. The letter begins to write itself, stroke by stroke.
She holds the haori up against the moon: for two seconds its rabbits and waves shine through onto the paper.
She lays it over the sleeping child; the shadows merge.
Stillness. Her hands in her lap. The moon is wholly inside the window by 131.

SHADOWS CAST BY NOTHING: a cloud with seven celestials and a canopied carriage slides down panels 2–3. The garden outside is empty; her real shadow does not move. The insects thin (8→3 voices by 138).
For 0.6 s the moon's maria shift into a figure under a katsura tree, beckoning (桂男) — then settle back into the rabbit.
A ribbon of light unfurls down the central stile and reaches her (139.8).

CULMINATION: the moon exactly centred in the round window. Her shadow peels off the paper and stands; its back straightens. The colour plates begin to drift out of register — the room trembles like eyes filling with tears; the moon grows blue and gold fringes. The koto begins to forget.
She climbs the kumiko rung by rung; each cell flashes as she passes; her hair lengthens into Heian hair; the ribbon winds round her.
At the top, under the window, she looks back once — against the rule of the myth. One E♭ on the koto: the ache, for a single note.
CLICK. Perfect register, sharp and cold. The koto stops on the rest where the fifth note should be.
She enters the moon (kira pinpoint 148.4). A black cloud covers the window; the shoji go dark. ABSOLUTE SILENCE (148.0–152.0).
The cloud passes; a breath of wind returns.
The moon alone in the window, a little right of centre. On the paper only the child's small shadow under the haori's. Her seated shadow is gone.
Shot A′ outside: たけ upright, eyes closed; the child asleep in her lap.
Her colour drains downward like moonlight — to 胡粉 and 銀鼠 — while the haori and the red obi-age stay bright.
One suzumushi. (158.2: another.) The child casts a shadow; the grandmother casts none.
KON.

segments.audio: 118–140: shō aitake (A4 B4 E5 F♯5 A5 B5) swells pp → f by 140. 122.5–130.5: under the letter, soft brush-on-paper swishes per character (band-passed noise 1.5–4 kHz, 80 ms) over a sustained koto D3 drone. 124.0–126.0: a quiet ascending koto glissando as the rabbits shine through. 132.0: kagura-suzu clusters pinned to the cloud shadow; insects thin 8→3 voices by 138. 136.0: a soft taiko heartbeat (55 Hz, 60 bpm) begins. 140.0–147.8 THE KOTO FORGETS in four passes: pass 1 at 140.0 A4 B♭4 D5 E♭5 — the fifth withheld, the shō fills the gap; pass 2 at 141.9 A4 B4 D5 E5 — semitones raised, heaven has no semitones; pass 3 at 143.8 D5 E5; pass 4 at 145.6 E5 alone, a thin harmonic. 147.0: at the look back, one E♭5 with oshide (pressed up from D5) — the ache returns for one note — and the heartbeat stops. 147.8: the kentō CLICK of 序 (dry, close, louder) and the rest where D5 should fall. 148.0–152.0: ABSOLUTE SILENCE — master gain 0, no insects, no wind, no reverb tail. 152.0: faint wind. 156.6: one suzumushi 'rīn'; 158.2: a second. 159.2: the sōzu trickle again. 160.0: KON.

segments.hero_image: 29s [147] — the round window with the full moon exactly centred behind a reed lattice; beneath it, at the top of the kumiko ladder, the shadow of a young woman with long Heian hair turns back toward the small shadow of a sleeping child under a haori; a white ribbon of light runs down the central stile; every colour plate trembles a few px out of register so the moon wears faint blue and gold fringes (homage: 芳年『月百姿』「月宮迎 竹とり」, transposed into shadow). Second image 40s [158]: an old woman drained to moon-white beside a sleeping child in a bright indigo haori and a red sash — one shadow on the boards.
segments.simplification: All of heaven is single-colour 藍鼠 shadow (no full-colour celestials). The climb is a 4-pose cycle. The colour drain is two offscreen renders of A′ (colour / drained) composited through a moving feathered gradient mask (destination-in) plus kira points on the front. Misregistration is the shared per-plate (dx,dy) table. The 桂男 flicker is a 0.6 s crossfade between two maria bitmaps.

segments.shot: A (後摺), A′ inserts, 月に雁 crop
segments.summary: The same garden pulled sixty years later from the worn blocks: no warm colours, a flat sky without bokashi, broken key lines, drifted registration, yellowed and foxed paper. Reeds have taken half the pond, the sōzu is dry, one shoji is torn. Only the moon is fresh. A bent figure in the rabbit-and-wave haori sits on the engawa — drawn on たけ's exact path — so for a moment we believe she has come back. She stacks fifteen dango to a koto that has lost some of its notes; she pours two cups of tea, and one stays untouched with a tiny moon in it. A faded pink cord ties the susuki: the child's obi-age. It is 小夜. A tall 月に雁 print: three geese cross the moon, the third lagging, with Bai Juyi's Mid-Autumn couplet as its inscription. Then her old hands make the fox window, and inside it the first impression is still playing — the warm andon, her grandmother, the little girl, who turns and looks out across sixty years. The hands tremble and come down.

beats.desc: KON. The print jolts 4–8 px; the warm blocks lift away; the key lines crack; the paper yellows (160.0–160.6).
The same garden, sixty years on. Only the moon is fresh. Three insects.
A bent figure in the 波兎 haori sits on the engawa — たけ's silhouette. We believe she has come back.
Fifteen dango, one per pluck, slower; four plucks are missing and those dango arrive in silence.
A′: old hands pour two cups of tea. One steams.
The other stays untouched; a tiny moon floats in it.
The faded pink cord tying the susuki — the child's obi-age. It is 小夜.
The margins close into a tall 月に雁 print; three geese cross the fresh moon; the third lags behind.
A′: 小夜's old hands form the fox window toward the moon.
Inside it the first impression is still playing: a small arm steals a dango; たけ turns to the moon.
Inside the window the little girl turns and looks straight out — across sixty years.
Inside, the andon goes out.
The hands tremble; the diamond shakes; they come down (189.0–190.0).

text_cues.reading: はおりきて　そぼのかたちに　つきをみる

text_cues.zh: 披上祖母的羽织——以她的身形，看月。
text_cues.note: かたち = both the garment's shape and the bent body: she has become the person she lost. 羽織 quietly rhymes with 羽衣. Kigo 月. Stays in the same place through the A′ insert, whose composition keeps x 500–860, y 60–580 plain. Ink dark: the 後摺 sky is pale.

segments.audio: 160.0: the jolt — a dry paper crack (high-passed noise burst, 60 ms) under the KON's tail. Insects: three voices only, sparse; thinner wind; NO sōzu trickle. 163.0–169.0: the counting melody of 一, slower (0.5 s spacing), plucks 3, 7, 10 and 13 deleted and every decay shortened (Karplus-Strong loss up): the melody as a late impression. 169.0: tea poured (filtered noise trickle, 1.2 s), a small ceramic tick; silence round the untouched cup (170.5). 171.0: a single koto B♭4, pressed softly (the cord). 173.0–182.0: distant geese — two-formant FM honks with delay at 174.5 and 176.0, and alone, late, at 178.4; a long shakuhachi A4 bending meri and back. 182.0: the fox-window cluster of 三 (A6 B6 E7) returns; inside the window, low-passed and quieter, the 初摺 soundscape of t−150 (the full insect chorus of 一; the andon breath at 187.0). 188.0–190.0: breathy shakuhachi muraiki as the hands tremble, then silence.

Second image 26.5s [186.5]: inside a diamond of old knuckled fingers, a warm lamplit engawa where a little girl turns to look straight out at us; everything outside the diamond is faded.
segments.simplification: Everything is reuse: Shot A with printState 'atozuri' (the per-plate table, dash-gapped key line, cached foxing), CAST.elder on たけ's path, the fox-window path from 三, and the inset is literally drawShotA(t−150,'shozuri') under a clip. The crop is two margin rectangles over a small bespoke composition.

segments.summary: The room is empty: no andon, no scroll — only a darker, unfaded rectangle where the scroll hung for decades. Through a torn panel a coin of moonlight falls on the tatami; through the open panel the moon hangs low and pale. 小夜 sits outside with her back to us and lights incense: a straight thread of smoke that stops short of the moon. She dozes. Two eye-glints at the edge of the engawa: the fox takes the top dango. She wakes, sees, and — exactly as たけ did — turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see.

She dozes; her head nods twice.
Two eye-glints at the edge of the engawa. A paw's shadow. The top dango is gone.
She wakes, turns to the stand, and sees.
She turns her face to the moon and pretends not to see — たけ's gesture, inherited. The tilt of her head suggests a smile.

A slow push-in on the smoke thread (scale 1.00→1.04 about (1180,700)).

text_cues.reading: ひとつへる　だんごのやまや　きょうのつき

text_cues.zh: 团子堆上，少了一个——今夜的月。
text_cues.note: Written as if on panel 1's paper. On the surface, the children's お月見泥棒 custom (tonight the thief is a fox); underneath, 'one fewer at the table'. Kigo 今日の月 (仲秋).

segments.audio: Only one or two insects left, far apart. Pre-dawn wind in sparse gusts. Single koto notes like drips: G4 at 191.0, D4 at 194.5, A4 at 200.0. 191.0: the faintest ember hiss. 196.0: a dry susuki rustle — the unseen thief. 198.5: at her pretended not-seeing, the same koto harmonic that marked たけ's complicity at 33.6. 201.5: a drop of dew falls into the dry sōzu — 'plink': the water beginning to return.
segments.transition_out: Match-cut at 206.0 (0 s): the incense thread at x 1180 cuts to Fuji's smoke thread rising at exactly the same x.
segments.hero_image: 9s [199] — a dim empty room; a pale rectangle on the wall where a scroll once hung; a coin of moonlight on the tatami through a torn shoji; through the open panel, a small old woman in a rabbit-and-wave haori, her back to us, her face turned to a low pale moon; one thread of incense rising straight.
segments.simplification: Shot B cached in the 後摺 state; panel 3 is simply not drawn (the opening shows a small bespoke exterior); the only animation is the thread (a sine-perturbed polyline), the figure's head (CAST.elder back view), the glints and one dango.

segments.print_state: atozuri + a fresh 東雲 block → unprinted
segments.summary: Dawn. Fuji from afar; the tiny house, one figure, the fox sitting in the susuki. The pale moon comes down toward the summit as a thread of smoke rises from the crater — the undying smoke of the burned elixir. At 214.0 the smoke touches the moon's rim: the only contact between earth and moon in the whole film. The shakuhachi, voice of the one left behind, finally plays the missing fifth note, and the first temple bell of dawn — held back all night — sustains it. 小夜's dawn shadow stretches across the susuki toward where たけ went. Then the print unprints itself in the real order in which pigments fade — reds first, then blues, then earths, sumi last — until only blank washi remains, the registration notch, and a moon embossed in the paper carrying nothing but the rabbit's faint carbon. Her last haiku writes itself beside it. A red seal: 忘れじ — I will not forget.

moon.phase_note: full, setting; 銀鼠/月白 glaze, kira fading, faint maria; after the unprinting it survives only as a karazuri circle at (960,360) r 150 with the rabbit's carbon at α 0.10

Each group slips 2–4 px out of register and rises 4 px as its alpha falls to 0 (inOutSine).

layers.description: Clean 生成 washi; the 見当 notch at (1840,1040) as in 序; a karazuri moon at (960,360), r 150 — a ±1.5 px rim (胡粉 highlight upper-left, 墨 α 0.12 shadow lower-right) and a faint inner sheen; inside it the rabbit's maria at 墨 α 0.10 (carbon does not fade). At 230.0 the scene stamps the 朱 seal 「忘れじ」 (≈90 px) at (1300,820). At 233.0 a tiny colophon in 墨 α 0.55, bottom-right (x 1500–1820, y 1000): 「原典　竹取物語・今昔物語集」.

beats.desc: Match-cut: Fuji's smoke continues the incense thread at x 1180. 東雲 rises at the left. The tiny house, one figure, the fox in the susuki.
The emperor's poem appears.
A thin koto offers the first four notes of the 縁 motif — A, B♭, D, E♭ — and waits.
The smoke touches the moon's lower rim — the only contact between earth and moon in the film; a kira flash runs round the rim. The SHAKUHACHI plays the missing D.
The first 梵鐘 of dawn (明け六つ), its hum tuned to D, sustains the note. 小夜's dawn shadow begins to stretch toward the mountain.
Pearl Fuji: the moon rests on the summit, the smoke rising into it.
The fox turns its head toward the peak.
The moon has sunk into the mountain; the smoke goes on rising into an empty sky.
Second bell.
The unprinting begins: reds and the dawn first … blues … earths … sumi last (228.0).
小夜's last haiku writes itself beside the embossed moon — the only new ink.
Third bell.
Blank washi, the registration notch, and a moon embossed in the paper with the rabbit's faint carbon.
A 朱 seal 「忘れじ」 is stamped — a soft taiko thud.
A last sōzu KON: the water has returned.
One suzumushi. The colophon. Silence to the end (236.0).

text_cues.reading: あふことも　なみだにうかぶ　わがみには　しなぬくすりも　なににかはせむ
text_cues.author: 帝　竹取物語
text_cues.source: 『竹取物語』帝の歌（かぐや姫の文と不死の薬を受けて）
text_cues.zh: 再也无缘相见，此身只在泪中浮沉——那不死之药，又有何用？
text_cues.note: On screen while the smoke of the burned elixir climbs to the moon; it fades just after the contact at 214.0.

ja: その煙、いまだ雲の中へ
立ち昇るとぞ、言ひ伝へたる。
text_cues.reading: そのけぶり、いまだくものなかへ　たちのぼるとぞ、いひつたへたる。
text_cues.author: 竹取物語
text_cues.zh: 据说，那烟至今仍向云中升腾。（富士，音同“不死”。）
text_cues.note: The tale's own etymology for 富士 is 士に富む (many soldiers climbed the mountain); the 不死 homophone is the famous pun and lives only in the Chinese gloss. Fades as the unprinting begins.

text_cues.reading: かげひとつ　こうしをのぼる　りょうやかな
text_cues.author: 小夜
text_cues.zh: 一道影子，攀上窗格——好一个良宵。
text_cues.note: Her poem about that night; the film ends in her voice. Kigo 良夜 (仲秋). 格子 instead of 障子 avoids a winter-kigo 季重なり. It writes itself while the world unprints — the only new ink — and stays to the last frame.

segments.negative_space: Upper-left x 100–520, y 50–470 (pale sky above the 東雲) for the emperor's waka; upper-right x 1560–1860, y 60–520 (sky right of the peak) for the narration; after the unprinting, the space right of the embossed moon x 1150–1440, y 150–780 for the final haiku, with the seal 忘れじ at (1300,820). Keep the moon's circle (x 810–1110, y 210–510) and the notch clear. Subtitle band y 960–1040: susuki, then bare paper.
segments.audio: Dawn pine-wind (soft low-passed noise); insects down to two voices. 210.5: thin koto (damped 後摺 decay) A4 · B♭4 · D5 · E♭5 — then the rest, waiting. 214.0: SHAKUHACHI D5, the missing fifth note: breathy muraiki onset, meri from C♯ up to D, then pure, held 6 s. 215.0 / 220.0 / 225.0: 梵鐘, three strokes of 明け六つ — inharmonic partials over a D hum (D3 146.8 Hz), one pair detuned 0.7 Hz for 唸り, 12 s decay; the first stroke's hum sustains the shakuhachi's D. 222.0–228.0: four soft paper-peel swishes as the plate groups lift. 230.0: the seal — soft taiko thud (55 Hz sine + felt click) and a paper press. 232.5: sōzu KON (the water has returned). 233.0: one suzumushi 'rīn' (1.2 s). 234.2–236.0: silence.
segments.transition_out: End of film at 236.0: hold on blank washi — the embossed moon, the haiku, the seal, the notch, the colophon — in silence; the engine's end card follows. No fade to black: the film ends on paper.
segments.hero_image: 10s [216] — pearl Fuji at dawn: a pale moon resting on the snow-capped summit, a single thread of smoke rising into it; 東雲 pink along the left horizon; far below, a tiny thatched house, a small fox in the susuki and one long shadow reaching toward the mountain (homage: 北斎『富嶽三十六景』; 芳年『月百姿』「烟中月」). Final frame 26s [232]: blank washi, an embossed moon with a faint rabbit, a vertical haiku and a red seal 忘れじ.
segments.simplification: Fuji is one polygon plus a snow polygon; the smoke is one tapered Bézier with glyphs; the unprinting is the shared per-plate alpha table (序's printing machinery run backwards in fugitive order); the karazuri moon is two 1 px arcs and a paper sheen; the seal is B.seal; the colophon is one ctx.fillText in the loaded mincho.

ending: The film ends on paper, not on black. After Fuji's smoke touches the moon (214.0) and the shakuhachi supplies the missing note under the first dawn bell, the whole print lifts away in the true order in which ukiyo-e pigments fade — safflower reds and the dawn first, then the blues, then the earths and greys, and the carbon key block last (222–228). What remains is blank washi with its registration notch and, at the place of culmination, a moon embossed into the paper without ink, still carrying the rabbit's faint smoke — the one thing that was given to the moon and kept. 小夜's haiku 「影ひとつ格子をのぼる良夜かな」 writes itself beside it, the only new ink; a red seal 「忘れじ」 (I will not forget) — the survivor's answer to the robe that erases grief — is pressed with a soft thud (230.0). A last sōzu KON: the water has returned to the dry bamboo. One suzumushi. A tiny colophon 「原典　竹取物語・今昔物語集」. Silence to 236.0.

fact_check: 『竹取物語』 quotations follow the standard 流布本 school text; kana (たまへ/給へ, 出で/いで, 立ち昇る/たち上る) varies by edition — lock every line to ONE edition (e.g. 新編日本古典文学全集) before release.

『今昔物語集』巻五第十三: the sentence 「万の人、月を見む毎に此の兎の事思ひ出づべし」 is the tale's closing line (preceded by the cloud-like shadows on the moon being the rabbit's smoke). Its final verb is 思出スベシ in the manuscript tradition and is normalised as 思ひ出づべし or 思ひいだすべし by different editors — choose one edition's reading.
芭蕉「名月や池をめぐりて夜もすがら」: 貞享三年（1686）八月十五夜、深川芭蕉庵の月見、『孤松』所収.
蕪村「月天心貧しき町を通りけり」: 明和五年（1768）; 月天心 after 邵雍《清夜吟》「月到天心処、風来水面時」.
白居易 couplet: from 「八月十五日夜禁中独直対月憶元九」; collected in 『和漢朗詠集』 under 十五夜; recited by Genji in 『源氏物語』須磨.
富士 naming: the tale itself derives 富士 from the many soldiers (士に富む) who climbed; 不死 is the celebrated homophone. The screenplay never claims the text says 不死.

Original haiku (all 5-7-5, each with an autumn kigo): 掬ひたる月こぼれけり子の手より (すくひたる/つきこぼれけり/このてより; 月) · 羽織着て祖母のかたちに月を見る (はおりきて/そぼのかたちに/つきをみる; 月) · ひとつ減る団子の山や今日の月 (ひとつへる/だんごのやまや/きょうのつき; 今日の月) · 影ひとつ格子をのぼる良夜かな (かげひとつ/こうしをのぼる/りょうやかな; 良夜). 障子 (winter) deliberately avoided.

Customs: fifteen 月見団子 stacked 9-4-2 (a common Kantō arrangement; regional variants exist); 衣かつぎ for 芋名月; お月見泥棒 is a regional children's custom; the fox-window chant varies too much by region and is never shown.
